questions.prompt: On an Abilene lot of five acres or less (including the parkway and alley), when do grasses, weeds, or brush become a nuisance?
choices: When they grow taller than 12 inches
When they grow taller than 6 inches
Any height is allowed if the lot is vacant
questions.answer: When they grow taller than 12 inches
questions.excerpt:
The purpose of this chapter is to protect the public health, safety, environment and
               general welfare of the citizens of the City of Abilene through the regulation of nuisances
               and illegal dumping. (Ord. No. 67-2006, pt. 1(Exh. A), 12-7-06)

Whereas, it is the desire of the City of Abilene Texas, to prevent the accumulation
               of abandoned or junked motor vehicles within the City, to eliminate the health and
               safety hazards associated with said vehicles and to abate the nuisances attributable
               to such vehicles, the City of Abilene hereby adopts V.T.C.A., Transportation Code
               Ch. 683, regarding "junked motor vehicles" in its entirety herein, and as amended,
               and it shall serve as the City's ordinance for said vehicles. An alternative administrative
               procedure as outlined in section 19-34 will be used in enforcing this section. (Ord. No. 67-2006, pt. 1(Exh. A), 12-7-06)

               chapter: Administrator. City of Abilene Peace Officers and Firefighters, Code Enforcement Officers, Environmental

                  alignment shall not be more than six (6) inches from the vertical measured at the
                  top of the fence; or (2) Has broken, loose, damaged, removed or missing parts including, but not limited to,
                  pickets, slats, posts, wood rails, bricks, and…

choices: On the grass in the front yard
On an improved parking surface such as concrete or asphalt, or behind an opaque fence that screens it from public view
Anywhere as long as it has current tags
Only if it is covered with a tarp
questions.answer: On an improved parking surface such as concrete or asphalt, or behind an opaque fence that screens it from public view

questions.prompt: Can you bring your own beer or wine to an Addison special event like Oktoberfest or Airfair Addison if alcohol is already being sold there?
choices: Yes, if it stays in a cooler
No, you may not bring, carry, or transport alcoholic beverages onto the site
Only if you also buy a drink at the event
questions.answer: No, you may not bring, carry, or transport alcoholic beverages onto the site
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 22; alcoholic beverages prohibited in parks, § 58-39. State Law reference— Local regulation of alcoholic beverages, V.T.C.A., Alcoholic Beverage Code § 109.31 et seq.

The following words, terms and phrases when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings
               ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different
               meaning: Special event means any event which is sponsored in whole or in part by the town. Special events
               shall include but not limited to: Airfair Addison, Founder's Day, Grand Prix, Oktoberfest
               and other events as designated by the city council. State license means a license issued by the state or one of its agencies. (Code 1982, § 3.1-1) Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.

Nothing in this chapter shall be construed or interpreted to conflict with the state
               Alcoholic Beverage Code, V.T.C.A., Alcoholic Beverage Code § 1.01 et seq. The provisions of this chapter shall be subject to the limitations of such
               code and such code shall control. The municipal court of the town shall have jurisdiction
               of any offense under this chapter and under state law only where the constitution
               and the general law of this state confer such jurisdiction thereon. (Code 1982, § 3.1-2) State Law reference— Preemptive nature of Alcoholic Beverage Code, V.T.C.A., Alcoholic Beverage Code § 1.06.

               under provisions of such code. (c) Upon collection of the applicable tax or as prescribed under this section, the city

questions.prompt: Can you possess or drink an alcoholic beverage in a public park in Balch Springs?
choices: Yes, if you stay in a picnic area
No — it is banned in public parks and on public property
Yes, if the container is sealed
questions.answer: No — it is banned in public parks and on public property
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 18.

(a) No person shall consume or possess an alcoholic beverage in a public park or on public
               property within the city. (b) A person commits an offense, without regard to his mental state, if he possesses or
               consumes an alcoholic beverage in a public park or on public property within the city. (Code 1984, § 9-3-1)

(a) No person, firm or corporation within the city may sell alcoholic beverages if his
               or her place of business is within 300 feet of a church, public school, private school,
               day-care center, child care facility, or public hospital. The measurement of the distance
               between the place of business where alcoholic beverages are sold and a church or public
               hospital shall be along the property lines of the street fronts and from front door
               to front door, and in a direct line across intersections. The measurement of the distance

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Local regulation of alcoholic beverages, V.T.C.A., Alcoholic Beverage Code § 109.31
               et seq.

For the purposes of this chapter, all definitions of words, terms and phrases as set
               forth in the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code are hereby adopted and made a part hereof. (Ord. No. 88-047, § 1, 11-7-1988)

The sale of alcoholic beverages by any dealer where the place of business of any such
               dealer is within 300 feet of any church, public school or public hospital, is hereby
               prohibited in accordance with the provisions of V.T.C.A., Alcoholic Beverage Code
               § 109.33. The distance between any such place of business and any church, public school
               or public hospital to be measured in accordance with said V.T.C.A., Alcoholic Beverage
               Code § 109.33. Provision is made, however, for the granting of a variance from the prohibition herein
               contained; a variance may be granted by the city council of the City of Bellaire,
               thus allowing the sale of alcoholic beverages within 300 feet of any church, public
               school or public hospital, if the city council determines that enforcement of the
               prohibition in a particular instance is not in the best interest of the public, constitutes
               waste or inefficient use of land or other resources, creates an undue hardship on
               an applicant for a license or permit, does not serve its intended purpose, is not

               XI, §§ 1.01 through 11.05. Amendments to the Charter are indicated by parenthetical
               history notes following amended provisions. The absence of a history note indicates
               that the provision remains unchanged from the original. Obvious misspellings have
               been corrected without notation. Additions made for clarity are indicated by brackets.

            government, provide for the future progress of our City, and obtain more fully the
            benefits of local self-government, do hereby adopt this Home Rule Charter in accordance
            with State law and do hereby declare the residents of the City of Colleyville in Tarrant
            County, Texas, living within the legally established boundaries of said City, to be

               from the original ordinance which was approved by the voters on January 15, 1977.

               Additions made for clarity are indicated by brackets [ ].

questions.prompt: How far outside Crystal City can the city regulate the platting and subdividing of land?
choices: One mile beyond the city limits
Five miles beyond the city limits
questions.answer: Five miles beyond the city limits
questions.excerpt:
The city shall have the power through the city council, with the aid of the planning
               and zoning commission, to adopt and enforce: (i) A master plan for the growth, development
               and beautification of the city, (ii) ordinances establishing rules and regulations
               governing the platting or subdividing of land, within the city and within all of the
               area extending five miles beyond the corporate limits (iii) ordinances dividing the
               city into zones or districts for the purpose of promoting the public health, safety,
               morals, order, convenience, prosperity and general welfare through the regulation
               and control of land use, the size, height, bulk and use of buildings within such zones
               or districts, and building setback lines, (iv) and any other ordinances, not in conflict
               with the constitution and laws of the State of Texas, which are needed to make fully
               effective the provisions of this article. Without any intent of limitation, but for the purpose of greater certainty the following
               described laws are hereby adopted as completely as if embodied herein: (1) Chapter 231, page 342, Acts of the 40th Legislature, 1927, being Article 974a, Vernon's
                  Texas Civil Statutes which authorizes the city to regulate and control the platting
                  and subdividing of land within the city and for five miles beyond the corporate limits. (2) Chapter 283, page 424, Acts of the 40th Legislature, 1927, being Articles 1011a to
                  1011j, inclusive, Vernon's Texas Civil Statutes which authorizes the city to adopt
                  zoning ordinances.

questions.prompt: Do restaurants, grocery stores, or food trucks in Deer Park need a city-issued alcohol permit if they already paid a food operating fee?
choices: Yes, they must get a separate city alcohol permit
No, no city-issued alcohol permit is required
Only if they also sell liquor
questions.answer: No, no city-issued alcohol permit is required
questions.excerpt:
(a) Pursuant to V.T.C.A., Texas Health and Safety Code, § 437.01235, as amended by Senate
               Bill 1008, a county, municipality, or public health district may not charge a fee
               under V.T.C.A., Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code (TABC), §§ 11.38 or 61.36 for a premises
               that is a food service establishment, retail food store, mobile food unit, roadside
               food vendor, or temporary food service establishment that has already paid a fee to
               operate to the state or to any county, municipality, or public health district. Thus
               SB 1008 has removed the ability for the city to collect the 50 percent of the state
               fee charged by the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) to provide a permit
               for entities that are described above. No city issued alcohol permit will be required
               for entities that are described above. (b) For entities that are not described by subsection (a), such as, but not limited to,
               liquor stores or bonded warehouses, the city retains the right to invoice for 50 percent
               of the state fee charged for these licenses as showed on the TABC website for the
               term of the TABC permit. (Code 1991, § 4-1; Code 2003, § 10-1; Code 2014, § 10-1; Ord. No. 4659 , § 1, 11-4-2025)

When an application is made to the state alcoholic beverage commission for a license
               or permit under this chapter, the city secretary shall certify whether the location
               or address given in the application is in a wet area and whether the sale of alcoholic
               beverages for which the permit is sought is prohibited by charter or ordinance. The
               fee for this certification shall be as provided in the fee schedule in appendix B
               to this Code. (Code 1991, § 4-2; Code 2003, § 10-2; Code 2014, § 10-2; Ord. No. 4659 , § 1, 11-4-2025)

questions.prompt: In Helotes, how large is the city's two-year permit fee for package stores and wine and beer retailers?
choices: Exactly half of the fee the state charges
The same as the state fee
questions.answer: Exactly half of the fee the state charges
questions.excerpt:
(a) A biennial permit fee equal in amount to exactly one-half of that levied by the state
               is hereby levied upon all package stores and upon all wine and beer retailers located
               within the limits of the City of Helotes for the use and benefit of the city. The
               fee shall be, and the same hereby is levied, on package stores, whether they sell
               all or any part of the classifications of intoxicating beverages, and upon wine and
               beer retailers upon the same basis, and whether holding a permit for sale of same
               for consumption on or off the premises. These fees are levied pursuant to the provisions
               of the "Alcoholic Beverage Code," Vernon's Amended Texas Statutes. (b) A biennial permit fee or gross receipts tax or occupation tax or other tax permitted
               by state law is hereby levied upon all businesses in the city in the business of selling
               mixed drinks in the manner and for the time and in the maximum amount permitted by
               state law. (c) Such permit fees and gross receipt taxes shall be paid to the city on or before the
               31st day of January in every odd numbered calendar year. (d) Upon payment of said permit fees and gross receipt taxes, the city alcoholic beverage
               sales license issued by the development services department shall be posted and displayed
               conspicuously with the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission License within the business. (Ord. No. 47, §1-3, 9-9-1987; Ord. 432, §1, 6-10-2010; Ord. No. 494, §1, 1-24-2013)

questions.prompt: What is the speed limit for driving on public streets in Hilshire Village?
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Uniform Act Regulating Traffic on Highways, Vernon's Ann. Civ. Stat., art. 6701d;
               Powers of local authorities, Vernon's Ann. Civ. Stat., art. 6701d, Sec. 27.

Footnotes: --- ( 2 ) --- State Law reference— Uniform Act Regulating Traffic on Highways, Vernon's Ann. Civ. Stat., art. 6701d;
               Powers of local authorities, Vernon's Ann. Civ. Stat., art. 6701d, Sec. 27.

(a) If any person while driving or operating any vehicle within the territorial limits
               of the City of Hilshire Village shall carelessly, recklessly or negligently collide
               with or cause injury to any person or property, or while driving or operating any
               motor vehicle within the territorial limits of the City of Hilshire Village shall
               carelessly, recklessly or negligently collide with or cause injury to another vehicle
               or property, he shall be deemed guilty of an offense. Proof of no intent to injure
               shall be no defense to a charge of violating the law. (b) The term "negligently" as used in subsection (a) of this section is defined to mean
               driving any vehicle which other than emergency vehicles at a greater speed than that
               allowed by law; or the violation of any traffic law of this state or city; or the
               failure to use that degree of care and caution that a man of ordinary care and prudence
               would use under the same or similar circumstances. (Ordinance 18 adopted 9/3/57, Section 2)

The driver of any vehicle involved in any collision with another vehicle or with a
               pedestrian shall immediately stop such vehicle at the scene of such accident or as
               close thereto shall remain at, the scene of the accident until he has fulfilled the
               requirements of Section 10.103 . Every such stop shall be made without obstructing traffic more than is necessary.…

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 1481 , § 1, adopted March 10, 2015, repealed former ch. 3 in its entirety, and enacted
               new provisions to read as herein set out. Former ch. 3, §§ 3-1—3-8, 3-20, 3-30—3-38,
               3-50—3-61, 3-71—3-74, 3-85—3-91 pertained to animal regulations. See the Code Comparative
               Table for a complete derivation.

The purpose of this chapter is to: (1) Prevent hazards to the physical and mental health of the public caused by animals; (2) Prevent cruelty to animals; (3) Decrease the number of unwanted and stray dogs and cats in the city; (4) Encourage responsible animal ownership; (5) Place the responsibility of complying with its requirements upon an animal's owner. ( Ord. No. 1481 , § 1, 3-10-15)

[The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning:] Abandon means the act of leaving an animal: (1) Without food, water or care for twenty-four (24) hours or more; or (2) In a situation where conditions present an immediate, direct, and serious threat to
                  the life, safety, or health of the animal. Altered means incapable of reproduction; synonym of sterilized, neutered or spayed. Animal means any warm or cold-blooded vertebrate. Animal control officer means the person designated by the city manager to represent and act for the city

We, the citizens of Keller, Texas, in order to establish a home rule municipal government,

The initial boundaries of the City of Keller shall be those of the City of Keller
               as of the date of adoption of this Charter.

               after publication of such notices and holding of such hearings as are required by
               law.

The city council may, after compliance with the notice provisions required by the
               Municipal Annexation Act for annexations, by ordinance disannex a portion of the city
               in order to adjust the city limits pursuant to a boundary agreement entered into with
               an adjacent city.

               privileges and immunities of every name and nature whatsoever now or hereafter granted
               to municipal corporations and the city by the Constitution and laws of the State of

               the powers, functions, rights, privileges and immunities granted.

questions.prompt: How close to a church, public school, or public hospital is selling alcohol banned in Lake Dallas?
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Local regulation of alcoholic beverages, V.T.C.A., Alcoholic Beverage Code §§ 11.38,

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: License means a license authorized by the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code. Permit means a permit authorized by the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code.

(a) The sale of alcoholic beverages by any dealer where the place of business of any such
               dealer is within 300 feet of any church, public school or public hospital is prohibited. (b) The measurement of the distance between the place of business where alcoholic beverages
               are sold and the church or public hospital shall be along the property lines of the
               street fronts and from front door to front door, and in direct line across intersections.
               The measurement of the distance between the place of business where alcoholic beverages
               are sold and the public schools shall be in a direct line from the property line of
               the public school to the property line of the place of business, and in a direct line
               across intersections. (c) The violation of this section is an offense punishable by a fine not exceeding $500.00,

(A) Use of motor brakes and certain sound amplification devices prohibited. (1) Use of motor brakes prohibited. Except as otherwise provided by division (B) below, no driver of a motor vehicle
               that is equipped with an engine or exhaust brake, or other similar device that uses
               engine compression to help slow the vehicle, shall use the engine or exhaust brake
               or other similar device in the City of Lindale. (2) Use of certain sound amplification devices on vehicles prohibited. Except as otherwise provided by division (B) below, no person shall operate a motor
               vehicle in the right-of-way of a street or highway within the City of Lindale and
               use a sound amplification device that can be heard at a distance of more than 25 feet
               from the vehicle. (B) Exemptions and affirmative defenses. (1) Exceptions. A person does not commit an offense under division (A)(2) above if: (a) The motor vehicle is an authorized emergency vehicle being used for emergency services; (b) The motor vehicle is an authorized law enforcement vehicle being used for law enforcement
               purposes; or (c) The motor vehicle is being used in a parade. (2) Affirmative defenses. (a) It is an affirmative defense to a charge under division (A)(1) above, that the driver
               was in an emergency situation and the use of the engine, exhaust brake or other similar
               device was necessary to avoid a collision or to keep the vehicle under control. (b) It is an affirmative defense to a charge under division (A)(2) above, that the sound
               amplification device was a horn or similar device used to warn of an emergency or
               hazardous situation. (Ord. 18-2004, passed 9-21-2004) Cross reference— Penalty, see § 70.99 .

               law, to collect. (b) Terms of license. (1) A license issued under the terms of this section shall terminate one year from the

questions.answer: on a collar or harness at all times

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Health and safety of animals, V.T.C.A., Health and Safety Code § 821.001 et seq.

(a) No owner shall have within the city any dog or cat four months of age or older unless

               tag issued by a city office designated by the chief of police to issue such registration
               tags, or a veterinarian authorized by the chief of police to issue the tag, must be
               affixed to a collar or harness that must be worn by the dog or cat at all times. No
               dog or cat shall be registered until it has a current vaccination. (1) Application for initial issuance or renewal of each registration must be made by the

               or unneutered animal. If the cat or dog being registered has been neutered or spayed
               and proof of such sterilization can be shown to the person designated to issue such
               registration or a veterinarian authorized to issue such registrations, a fee of $5.00
               will be charged. Dogs and cats under the age of one year shall be registered at the
               sterilized fee. Animals may be exempted from the sterilization provision upon written
               recommendation from a veterinarian that such alteration would be harmful or dangerous

            The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion.
            In the case of a title of the republication, the number to the left of the colon indicates

            to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. Index or Indexes The index has been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been

            City of Round Rock, Williamson County, Texas, residing within the legally established
            boundaries of said City, to be a political subdivision of the state of Texas incorporated

            as are herein provided. (Charter amendment approved by voters January 20, 1996; May 6, 2000) Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Note— Printed in this part is the Home Rule Charter of the city, which was approved at an

               municipality, V.T.C.A., Local Government Code ch. 9.

questions.prompt: In Taylor, selling alcoholic beverages is unlawful if the business is within 300 feet of a church that is not located where?
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Food and food handlers, Ch. 10.

(a) The sale within the corporate limits of the city, of any alcoholic beverage by any
               dealer where the place of business of any such dealer is within 300 feet of any church,
               if the church is not located in the Central Business District, or a public school
               or a public hospital shall be unlawful. No distance requirements from a church in
               the Central Business District are imposed for the sale of alcoholic beverages from
               the place of business by any dealer. (b) As used in this section the term "alcoholic beverage" shall mean alcohol and any beverage
               containing more than one-half of one percent of alcohol by volume which is capable
               of use for beverage purposes, either alone or when diluted. As used in this section
               the term "dealer" shall mean any person who deals in alcoholic beverages and shall
               include a permittee or licensee who has paid the city the fee levied by the city for
               permits or licenses to sell alcoholic beverages in city. (Ord. of 3-25-1941, §§ 1—4; Ord. No. 2014-08 , § 2, 6-26-2014) State Law reference— Location restrictions authorized, V.T.C.A. Alcoholic Beverage Code, § 109.33.

questions.prompt: Where are Uvalde’s official street monuments set?
choices: Right on the official street line
Three feet from the street line toward the center of the street
On private property next to the sidewalk
At the center of the street
questions.answer: Three feet from the street line toward the center of the street
questions.excerpt:
The Book of City Block Maps and General Street Profile and Cross Sections, as prepared
               by Bartlett & Ranney, Consulting Engineers, San Antonio, Texas, and as subsequently
               amended and added to under direction of the city council, are declared to be the official
               city street records of the city, and shall be kept on file for public inspection in
               the office of the city secretary. (Prior code § 22-1)

The lines and grades, as fixed by the official city street records referred to in
               Section 12.04.010 are declared to be the official street lines and grades for those streets in the
               city which are covered thereby. (Prior code § 22-2)

The monuments, as established by Bartlett & Ranney, and as subsequently added to and
               extended by the city engineer, shall fix the official street lines only, being set
               at a distance of three feet from the street line toward the center of the street.
               Any person who shall damage or move any official monument shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. (Prior code § 22-3)

All street improvements, except sidewalks and curbs, shall be made to conform with
               the lines as fixed in the official records referred to in Section 12.04.010 and by the street monuments referred to in Section 12.04.030 , and no improvements shall be permitted to project over such lines into the street
               without the consent of the city council. (Prior code § 22-4)

All sidewalks and curbs within the city limits shall be laid so as to conform, both
               as to line and grade, with the official lines and grades as shown in the official
               city street records referred to in Section 12.04.010 , which shall be located under the direction of the city engineer. (Prior code § 22-5)

The city shall, upon application to the city engineer, furnish lines and grades for
               sidewalks, curbs or other…

questions.prompt: Are you allowed to possess or drink alcohol in Venus city parks or on the city square?
choices: No, unless a special event permit allows it
Beer is allowed but not liquor
questions.answer: No, unless a special event permit allows it
questions.excerpt:
(a) All city parks and the city square are to be regulated by this chapter. (b) Alcoholic beverages are prohibited and may not be possessed and/or consumed on the
               city square or in the city parks except as otherwise authorized by this chapter. (c) Alcohol can be possessed and consumed in conjunction with a special event permit issued
               by the city that contains all necessary information about the use of alcohol and is
               in accordance with current state and/or federal law. Event organizers are required
               to hire off-duty city police officers through the method prescribed by the chief of
               police and will abide by any other stipulations as required by the city to ensure
               public safety. Event organizers will additionally comply with all provisions of the
               special event permit ordinance. (d) Any person violating the provisions of this chapter shall be deemed to be guilty of
               a misdemeanor and upon conviction shall be fined in an amount not less than $50.00
               nor more than $500.00. Each violation of this chapter shall be deemed a separate offense
               and each day that the violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense. Nothing
               in this chapter shall prevent the enforcement of this chapter by another means authorized
               by law, and this chapter may be enforced by any or all means, and the choice of one
               remedy is not to the exclusion of any other remedy. (Ord. No. 163-93, §§ 1, 4, 4-13-1993; Ord. No. 795-2024-03 , § 1, 3-25-2024)

               recommending to the city council, regulations creating zones within the city. (Ord. No. 20090113-2, § 1, 1-13-2009)

The name of the commission shall be the "City of Woodville Zoning Commission." (Ord. No. 20090113-2, § 1, 1-13-2009)

(a) The commission shall consist of seven commissioners appointed by the city council.
               Each councilman shall appoint one commissioner and the mayor shall appoint two commissioners.
               All commissioners shall reside within the limits of the City of Woodville. (b) Commissioners shall serve at the will of the city council and shall be appointed for
               two-year terms. Commissioners may be removed with or without cause by a majority vote
               of the councilmen at a regularly scheduled council meeting. (Ord. No. 20090113-2, § 1, 1-13-2009)

               but the city council shall be the sole authority as to whether such recommendations
               are adopted.
